documents.title: District Accessibility Policy Manual
documents.content:
Maplewood School District
District Accessibility Policy Manual
Version 2024.3
Effective: January 15, 2024
Issued by: District Accessibility Office
Supersedes: Version 2024.2 (October 2023)

This manual establishes the criteria and procedures for determining eligibility for physical accessibility accommodations within Maplewood School District. It applies to all students, parents, guardians, staff, and members of the public who access District facilities, programs, or activities. All District staff are expected to be familiar with the contents of this manual.

Maplewood School District has_policy_version 2024.3. Record status: current. This is the current version of the policy manual. All previous versions are maintained in the District Accessibility Office archive for reference and audit purposes.

SECTION 1: PURPOSE AND SCOPE

1.1 Purpose. The purpose of this manual is to ensure that all individuals are provided with equal opportunity to access District programs, services, and facilities. The District is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities, as defined in this manual.

1.2 Scope. This manual applies to all District-owned, leased, or operated facilities; all District-sponsored programs and activities; and all communications and interactions with the public. It governs the process by which individuals may request accommodations and the criteria by which such requests are evaluated.

1.3 Guiding Principles. The District shall:
(a) Provide accommodations that are effective in affording equal access;
(b) Ensure that accommodations are provided in the most integrated setting appropriate;
(c) Engage in an interactive process with individuals requesting accommodations;
(d) Maintain the confidentiality of medical and disability-related information, in accordance with applicable law.

SECTION 2: DEFINITIONS

2.1 Disability. A physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities, a record of such an impairment, or being regarded as having such an impairment. Major life activities include, but are not limited to, caring for oneself, performing manual tasks, seeing, hearing, eating, sleeping, walking, standing, lifting, bending, speaking, breathing, learning, reading, concentrating, thinking, communicating, and working. Major life activities also include the operation of a major bodily function.

2.2 Qualified Individual. An individual who, with or without reasonable accommodation, meets the essential eligibility requirements for receipt of services or participation in a District program or activity.

2.3 Reasonable Accommodation. A modification or adjustment to a policy, practice, procedure, or physical feature of a facility that enables a qualified individual with a disability to have equal access to District programs and activities. This may include the provision of auxiliary aids and services, modification of policies, or removal of architectural barriers.

2.4 Architectural Barrier. A physical feature of a facility that impedes access by an individual with a disability, including but not limited to steps, narrow doorways, inaccessible restrooms, inadequate signage, and uneven walking surfaces.

2.5 Auxiliary Aids and Services. Services or devices that enable effective communication, including qualified interpreters, assistive listening devices, captioning, Braille materials, large print materials, and screen-reading software.

documents.content:
**7. Appeals of Eligibility Determinations and Accommodation Decisions**

**7.1 Right to Appeal.** Any individual who has applied for accessibility services or accommodations through the District Accessibility Office (DAO), or who is the parent, guardian, or authorized representative of such an individual, may appeal an eligibility determination, an accommodation decision, a denial, a modification, or a termination of an approved accommodation plan. This right of appeal extends to determinations made by DAO staff and to decisions made by the Eligibility Review Committee (ERC) on reconsideration. The purpose of an appeal is to ensure that all determinations are made in accordance with this Policy Manual, applicable federal and state law, and the individual's documented needs.

**7.2 Appeal Levels.** The District provides two levels of appeal:

(a) *First Level Appeal – Reconsideration by the DAO Director.* A first level appeal is a request for reconsideration of an eligibility determination or accommodation decision made by DAO staff. The appeal must be submitted in writing to the DAO office. The DAO Director, or the Director's designee, shall review the appeal and issue a written decision within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of the appeal. The Director may affirm, reverse, or modify the original determination, or may remand the matter to the original reviewer for further documentation or evaluation.

(b) *Second Level Appeal – Review by the Eligibility Review Committee.* A second level appeal is a request for review of a decision made by the DAO Director on a first level appeal. The appeal must be submitted in writing to the DAO office using the Request for Eligibility Review form (Form DAO-7). The ERC shall review the matter in accordance with Section 6 of this Policy Manual. The ERC's decision on a second level appeal is final and shall not be subject to further internal appeal within the District, except as provided in Section 7.8 below regarding material change in circumstances.

**7.3 Time Limits for Filing Appeals.** The following time limits shall apply to all appeals:

(a) A first level appeal must be received by the DAO office no later than thirty (30) calendar days after the date of the written determination being appealed. The date of the determination is the date stamped on the notice of determination sent to the individual.

(b) A second level appeal must be received by the DAO office no later than fifteen (15) business days after the date of the DAO Director's written decision on the first level appeal.

(c) The DAO Director may extend the time limits for filing an appeal for good cause shown. A request for an extension must be made in writing and must state the reasons for the delay. The Director shall issue a written decision on the request for an extension within five (5) business days of receipt.

**7.4 Content of an Appeal.** An appeal must be in writing and must include the following information:

(a) The name, address, telephone number, and email address of the individual filing the appeal and, if applicable, the name and contact information of the parent, guardian, or authorized representative;

(b) The date of the determination or decision being appealed, and a copy of the notice of determination if available;

(c) A statement of the specific reasons why the individual believes the determination or decision is incorrect, including any additional information, documentation, or evaluation that was not previously considered;

**Section 8: Responsibilities of School Principals and Facilities Staff** (continued)

**8.3 Responsibilities of the Facilities and Maintenance Department.** The Facilities and Maintenance Department shall:

(a) Maintain a current inventory of all accessibility features at each school, including but not limited to ramps, automatic door openers, accessible restrooms, elevators, and visual fire alarm systems. The inventory shall be reviewed and updated at least annually, and whenever a significant alteration or repair is made to a building;

(b) Respond to work orders related to accessibility features in accordance with the priority schedule set forth in Section 8.4 below;

(c) Conduct an annual accessibility walk-through of each school in cooperation with the school's Accessibility Coordinator. The walk-through shall be documented on the form titled "Annual Accessibility Walk-Through Report" and a copy shall be provided to the DAO by May 31 of each year;

(d) Ensure that temporary barriers or hazards (e.g., construction debris blocking a ramp, snow accumulation at an entrance) are removed or mitigated within a reasonable time, not to exceed two (2) school days, except in cases of emergency;

(e) Notify the DAO within five (5) business days of any planned construction or renovation project that may affect the accessibility of a building or any part of a school facility.

**8.4 Work Order Priority Schedule.** The following priority levels shall be used by the Facilities and Maintenance Department when responding to work orders involving accessibility features:

Priority 1 – Immediate/Urgent. Conditions that pose an imminent safety risk or that prevent an individual from entering or exiting a building or accessing a required service (e.g., elevator out of service, ramp blocked, door opener not functioning). Response time: begin work within two (2) hours of notification during normal business hours; otherwise, as soon as possible. The school principal and the DAO shall be notified immediately.

Priority 2 – High. Conditions that significantly impair access but do not create an imminent safety risk (e.g., accessible restroom out of order, braille signage missing). Response time: begin work within one (1) business day.

Priority 3 – Routine. Conditions that are non-urgent but still affect accessibility (e.g., worn edge trim on a ramp, slow-closing automatic door). Response time: begin work within five (5) business days.

Priority 4 – Scheduled. Conditions that are identified during annual walk-throughs or planned maintenance and do not require immediate attention. These items shall be scheduled and completed within ninety (90) calendar days, unless otherwise approved by the DAO.

**8.5 Documentation of Work Orders.** All work orders related to accessibility features shall be documented in the District's work order management system. The documentation shall include, at a minimum: the date the work order was submitted, the name of the submitter, the location of the issue, a description of the issue, the priority level assigned, the date work was initiated, the date work was completed, and the name of the staff member who completed the work. A copy of any completed work order that involved a Priority 1 or Priority 2 condition shall be forwarded to the DAO promptly upon completion.

**Section 9: Documentation and Record-Keeping.**

**9.1 Eligibility Determination Record.** For each application for an accommodation, the DAO shall create and maintain an official record titled "Eligibility Determination Record" (EDR). The EDR shall be the single authoritative record of the eligibility determination process for that application. The EDR shall include, at a minimum:

documents.content:
**Section 9: Documentation and Record-Keeping (continued)**

**9.2 Inspection Forms and Photographs.** All accessibility inspections conducted by the DAO or its designees shall be documented on the District's standard Accessibility Inspection Form (AIF). Each AIF shall include the date of inspection, the name of the inspector, the facility name and address, the specific location within the facility, and a description of each condition observed. Photographs shall be taken of any condition that constitutes a Priority 1 or Priority 2 finding, and shall be referenced on the AIF by photograph number. Photographs shall be retained with the AIF and shall be considered part of the official record. The DAO may require photographs for any other condition as deemed necessary.

**9.3 Work Order Log.** The DAO shall maintain a master Work Order Log for all accessibility-related work orders. The log shall be updated within two (2) business days of any event requiring an entry. The log shall include the work order number, the date of submission, the priority level, the location, a brief description of the work, the date initiated, the date completed, and the name of the assigned staff member. The log shall be reviewed quarterly by the DAO to identify recurring issues or patterns.

**9.4 Record Retention.** All records described in this Section 9, including EDRs, AIFs, photographs, work orders, and the Work Order Log, shall be retained for a minimum of seven (7) years from the date of creation. Records related to a pending appeal or litigation shall be retained until the matter is fully resolved, even if the resolution occurs after the seven-year period. Records may be stored in electronic format, provided that the storage system preserves the integrity of the original document and permits accurate reproduction.

**Section 10: Definitions.**

For the purposes of this Policy Manual, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:

**10.1 Accessible Parking Space.** An accessible parking space is a designated parking space that complies with the applicable standards of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and the District's adopted building code. A space shall be considered accessible only if it meets all of the following criteria: (a) it is located on the shortest accessible route of travel to an accessible entrance; (b) it is of sufficient width and length to accommodate a vehicle with a side- or rear-mounted lift or ramp, as applicable; (c) it is served by an access aisle of the required width; (d) it has the required van-accessible clearance; and (e) it is identified by the required signage, including the International Symbol of Accessibility, mounted at the correct height and location. A space that is merely striped or marked but does not meet all of these criteria shall not be counted as an accessible parking space for purposes of this Policy.

**10.2 Path of Travel.** The path of travel is the continuous, unobstructed route of pedestrian travel within a facility or between a facility and a public way. The path of travel includes the accessible route, parking access aisles, curb ramps, walks, ramps, and the accessible entrance. A path of travel shall be considered accessible if it meets the applicable standards for width, slope, surface, and clearance, and if it does not contain any obstacle that would prevent a person with a disability from using it. A path of travel that is blocked by a temporary condition, such as construction or a parked vehicle, shall be considered inaccessible unless an equally accessible alternate route is provided and clearly marked.

documents.content:
WILLOW CREEK MIDDLE SCHOOL
Facilities & Maintenance Department
Work Order System

WORK ORDER NO: 2024-0418-A
DATE INITIATED: 04/22/2024
LOCATION: Willow Creek Middle School, 1400 Maple Ave., Bldg. A, Elevator #1 (north stairwell, near Gym B)

REQUESTED BY: S. Miller, Head Custodian
APPROVED BY: J. O'Neill, Facilities Supervisor
DATE APPROVED: 04/22/2024

PRIORITY: 1 – URGENT (Elevator out of service; student with mobility impairment affected)

TYPE OF WORK: Elevator repair / diagnostic
PROBLEM DESCRIPTION:
Elevator stuck between first and second floor around 7:45 AM. Door will not open. Reported by Ms. Rivera (front office) when student could not exit. No passengers currently inside. LED panel on first floor shows fault code E-12 (door lock circuit). Car is not responding to call buttons. Estimated age of unit: 12 yrs. Last PM service 03/28/2024 (see PM log).

STATUS: OUT OF SERVICE (elevator is not operational and shall remain locked out until repairs are completed and inspected)

EQUIPMENT TAG: ELEV-WC-001
MANUFACTURER: Otis Gen2
SERIAL: 74-G2-8891
CONTRACT VENDOR: Midwest Elevator Service (contract #MES-2210)

SCHEDULED WORK:
- Vendor to dispatch technician on 04/23/2024 between 8:00 AM and 12:00 PM.
- Replace door lock relay if diagnostic confirms fault.
- Test all floor landings for leveling and door reopen.

SAFETY NOTICE:
Elevator is posted with "OUT OF SERVICE" signage on all floor call panels. Power to car will remain ON (for lighting) but main control switch is in OFF position. Do not attempt to reset fault code without vendor authorization.

HISTORY (last 3 work orders for this unit):
- WO 2024-0210: 02/14/2024 – Door sensor adjusted, no parts. Status: completed
- WO 2023-1187: 11/30/2023 – Hydraulic leak on piston, gasket replaced. Status: completed
- WO 2023-0992: 09/15/2023 – Floor selector recalibrated. Status: completed

Willow Creek Middle School has_elevator_operational out_of_service. Record status: current.

COMMENTS / NOTES:
S. Miller reports the elevator has been "acting up" for about 2 weeks – occasional hesitation when arriving at second floor. Did not log a work order at the time because it seemed intermittent. Advised to log any vibration or delay immediately in the future.

TECHNICIAN ASSIGNMENT (vendor):
- Name: T. Hendricks
- Phone: (555) 214-8890
- PO #: 2024-5521

ATTACHMENTS:
- Photo of LED fault code (taken by S. Miller, phone photo, attached to this WO as digital file: WC-ELEV-0418.jpg)
- Floor plan for machine room access (key in main office lockbox #3)

APPROVAL SIGNATURE (J. O'Neill):
______________________________________
Date: 04/22/2024

COPY TO: S. Miller (custodial), Ms. Rivera (front office), M. Tran (ADA coordinator), Vendor file

END OF WORK ORDER – STATUS: OUT OF SERVICE (current, 04/22/2024)

---

ADDENDUM 1 – (added 04/23/2024, by J. O'Neill)
Technician T. Hendricks arrived 9:10 AM. Diagnosed failed door lock relay (part #OT-7712). Relay ordered, ETA 04/25/2024. Temporary repair attempted (bypass relay) but not approved for passenger use. Elevator remains OUT OF SERVICE. Will update when part arrives.

---

ADDENDUM 2 – (added 04/25/2024, by J. O'Neill)
Part arrived 10:30 AM. Hendricks replaced relay and ran full cycle test (all floors, door reopen, emergency alarm). Elevator passed. Reopened for normal use at 1:15 PM 04/25/2024. Work order closed.

FINAL STATUS: COMPLETED (elevator operational as of 04/25/2024)
Note: This document reflects the elevator's status as OUT OF SERVICE during the period 04/22/2024 through 04/25/2024, and operational thereafter.

WILLOW CREEK MIDDLE SCHOOL
FACILITIES & MAINTENANCE DEPARTMENT

MANUFACTURER: Otis
MODEL: 2000 Series

REQUESTED BY: S. Miller (Custodial)
APPROVED BY: J. O'Neill (Facilities Supervisor)
PRIORITY: URGENT – ELEVATOR OUT OF SERVICE

DESCRIPTION OF ISSUE:
Elevator reported out of service as of 04/22/2024. Per initial work order 2024-0228,
intermittent hesitation at second floor noted over the past two weeks, escalating to
complete failure on 04/22/2024. LED fault code displayed on controller (see attached
photo WC-ELEV-0418.jpg). Elevator will not move from first floor, doors will not close
fully. No passengers were trapped at time of failure.

WORK PERFORMED (04/23/2024):
Technician T. Hendricks arrived on site at 9:10 AM. Performed diagnostic testing on
controller, door lock circuit, and safety circuit. Fault code identified as E-27
(door lock relay failure). Tested relay with multimeter – no continuity. Door lock
relay (part #OT-7712) is defective. Relay ordered from vendor, ETA 04/25/2024.

Temporary bypass of relay was attempted to allow elevator to move for testing
purposes only. Bypass was NOT approved for passenger use. Elevator remained OUT OF
SERVICE. All doors were locked and elevator was placed on maintenance mode.

PARTS USED:
- Part #OT-7712 – Door lock relay (replacement), Qty 1
  Ordered 04/23/2024, received 04/25/2024 10:30 AM

WORK PERFORMED (04/25/2024):
Technician T. Hendricks arrived 10:45 AM. Replaced defective door lock relay with
new part #OT-7712. Reconnected all wiring, verified torque on terminal screws.
Performed full cycle test:
- All floors (1st, 2nd, 3rd) – pass
- Door reopen function – pass
- Door close safety edge – pass
- Emergency alarm – pass
- Emergency phone – pass
- Fire recall mode – pass
- Leveling accuracy – within 1/4 inch

Elevator passed all tests. Reopened for normal use at 1:15 PM 04/25/2024.

STATUS: COMPLETED – ELEVATOR OPERATIONAL AS OF 04/25/2024

FOLLOW-UP RECOMMENDATIONS:
1. Monitor door lock relay operation over next 30 days. If any intermittent
   hesitation returns, log immediately.
2. Schedule preventive maintenance on door lock mechanism within 90 days.
3. Clean controller cabinet and check all connections during next scheduled PM.

HISTORY (last 3 work orders for this unit):

- WO 2023-1187: 11/30/2023 – Hydraulic leak on piston, gasket replaced. Status: completed
- WO 2023-0992: 09/15/2023 – Floor selector recalibrated. Status: completed

it seemed intermittent. Advised to log any vibration or delay immediately in the future.
